title: Classification
subtitle: Logistic regression, decision boundaries, and class probabilities

content.text: Classification predicts a discrete label (spam/not-spam, cat/dog). Logistic regression outputs a probability that is thresholded to produce a class.

content.code:
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report

model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

preds = model.predict(X_test)
probs = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]  # probability of class 1

print(classification_report(y_test, preds))

content.text: Adjust the classification threshold (default 0.5) based on the cost of false positives vs false negatives.

questions.question: What does logistic regression output before thresholding?
questions.explanation: Logistic regression outputs a probability; the class label is determined by a threshold (usually 0.5).

faq.q: How do I handle imbalanced classes?
faq.a: Use class_weight="balanced" in scikit-learn, or oversample the minority class with SMOTE.
